claims.text: This is a single trip on the record, so the rider's initial burden of identity under POL-RD-08(a) is met: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-09113, and the trip_record's started_at (2026-09-20T18:20:00+08:00) matches the trace's first_fix_at to the second. There is no identifier mismatch and nothing to escalate under the identity limb.

The governing measurement is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 18.0 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 10.0 km, an excess of 8.0 km, or 80% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass with room to spare — the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km absolute — so a route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a max_gap_sec of 0. None of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires, so the excess stands on the trace alone and no independent corroborating artifact is required.

The rider accepts the closure, and the closure is real: LTA advisory ADV-20260920-113 names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, its validity window overlaps the trip, and it records a shortest lawful alternative of 12.0 km. But POL-RD-03 exoneration is capped, not open-ended: the justified excess is min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, and everything above that cap is the driver's to answer for.

Applying the POL-RD-03 cap produces a closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km (duration scaled to 27.2 minutes), and the trip still ran 18.0 km on the trace. The excess remaining after adjustment is 4.40 km — about 32% of the adjusted optimal and far above the 0.8 km absolute floor — so the deviation is still established on the adjusted route and the driver is not excused for it.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation runs against the closure-adjusted route, because POL-RD-03 excuses only part of the excess: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x surge 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the on-optimal-route gantry = 23.416 recompated against a charged_total of 31.42. The refund is therefore 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded UP to 8.05 payable.

The 8.004 refund is neither de minimis nor a full refund: it clears the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and at 25.5% of charged_total it falls well short of the 90% full-refund share, so the correct monetary outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-RD-02 — and because the payable figure rounds up to 8.05, it returns to the rider the entire SGD 8.05 that is contested in this dispute.

The only rider instruction on this record authorises the LAWFUL diversion, not an 18 km detour: at 18:23:10 the rider wrote 'please take the lawful diversion', and the shortest lawful alternative was 12.0 km. POL-RD-04 exonerates only the excess attributable to a rider instruction, so it cannot carry the 4.40 km of excess beyond the closure-adjusted route — the rider authorised the diversion, not an overrun of it.

POL-RD-04 is in any event unavailable to the driver on this record: neither chat message carries a waypoint_hint and the rider names no road, so the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 is undecidable, the clause cannot be run, and the case must be decided on the remaining clauses.

The rider's profile does not import any extra corroboration burden into POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the threshold of 4, so this claim is not one of those that must be supported beyond the gps_trace.

The S$2.80 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is flagged on_optimal_route false and is already comprehended inside the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which credits only the S$1.00 on-optimal-route gantry. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is itemised for transparency but must not be added on top of the 8.05 payable, and equally must not be netted down against it.

No part of this argument rests on discounted evidence: every artifact cited here carries admissibility status COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes, so no POL-GEN-02 disclosure discount applies and the deciding facts are carried by clean evidence.

claims.text: The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 is a genuine external closure and exonerates part of the excess under POL-RD-03: it names 'Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector', a segment the booked optimal route traverses (the trip record's route source states the optimal was computed 'via Pelton Canal Link, the segment named in the LTA advisory'), its geometry intersects the route, and its 18:14-18:55 SGT validity window covers the 18:20-18:54 SGT trip. The justified excess is capped at min(8.0 km, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, so 3.60 km of the 8.0 km excess is excused and only the residual 4.40 km can be refunded to the rider.

Materiality under POL-RD-01 is assessed on the excess REMAINING after the POL-RD-03 adjustment, not on the excess as first measured. The surviving excess is 4.40 km against a closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km, i.e. 32.4%, which is below the 50% limb, and 4.40 km is also below the 8.0 km absolute limb. The deviation is therefore established but NOT material on this record, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile consequences and any driver-conduct referral are not triggered by this trip.

Even if POL-RD-06 is reached, no repeat-deviation pattern exists: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, which is not 3 or more, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d (610) is 0.00, which is not 0.05 or more, with completed_trips_90d far above the 40-trip floor. The lifetime counter driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are available on this profile.

Once POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess, POL-RD-02 requires the fare to be recomputed against the closure-adjusted optimal route of 13.60 km / 27.2 min, not the booked 10.0 km / 20 min. On the adjusted route the recomputed fare is 23.416 (3.80 base + 10.20 distance + 7.616 time + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP; no surge, no promo, no waiting fee), so the refund is 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05 - the figure the fare breakdown already carries. Running the same clause against the booked optimal would yield 12.72 and would over-refund the rider by 4.72.

The off-route ERP line of SGD 2.80 at the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry (flagged on_optimal_route false) is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, which rebuilds the fare using only the on-optimal-route gantries (SGD 1.00 at the Pelton lawful diversion entry). Under POL-RD-09(1) the off-route charge is itemised for transparency but must NEVER be added on top of the refund, so the rider's total recovery on this dispute is capped at the POL-RD-02 figure.

The GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 - 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage and a maximum gap of 0 seconds - so it is impaired under none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation trigger is not engaged. The excess is accordingly measured exactly at 8.0 km on the governing trace distance, and nothing in the record supports a finding of any excess larger than the 4.40 km that survives the closure exoneration.

The chat log corroborates limb (c) of POL-RD-03 - that the actual route left the optimal corridor for the signed diversion and rejoined it - and dispels any suggestion of a driver frolic: at 18:22:40 the driver messaged that the Pelton Canal Link closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop, and at 18:23:10 the rider replied 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion.' The fare breakdown independently records the diversion-entry gantry as on the optimal route and the industrial-loop exit gantry as off it, matching the signed diversion the advisory describes.

The driver has discharged the burden that shifts to him under POL-RD-08 by naming a specific artifact and a specific clause - the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 and POL-RD-03 - rather than making a bare assertion that traffic was bad. The exoneration that follows is capped at 3.60 km, so the only sum properly refundable to the rider is the residual 4.40 km already reflected in the SGD 8.05 figure, and no greater sum may be awarded.

The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-09113-01) is a genuine external closure: it names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, a segment the booked optimal route traverses, its 18:14-18:55 window covers the 18:20-18:54 trip, and the actual route leaves the corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after. POL-RD-03 therefore excuses part of the excess, but only up to its cap: min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km / 27.2 min. The residual 4.40 km still clears POL-RD-01, so a refund is due; it is below both the 50% and the 8.0 km materiality limbs, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged - and in any event the driver's profile shows no repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral). POL-RD-02 recomputation against the adjusted route: 3.80 + (0.75 x 13.60 = 10.20) + (0.28 x 27.2 = 7.616) = 21.616; + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP = recomputed fare 23.416 against a charged total of 31.42. Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05 - a partial refund, since it clears the 0.50 de-minimis floor and is only 25.5% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share. The SGD 2.80 off-route 'Industrial loop exit' ERP is already comprehended in that figure (POL-RD-09(1)) and is not added on top. POL-RD-04 adds nothing: neither chat message carries a waypoint_hint and the rider names no road, so its corroboration test cannot be run and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. ruling.explanation:
To both parties.

Identity and trace quality. All three platform artifacts carry the same trip id TRP-09113 and the trip_record's start (18:20:00) matches the trace's first fix, so there is no identity problem to escalate. The GPS trace is complete — 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, a max gap of 0 — so it is impaired under none of POL-RD-07(a)-(c) and the distance it records stands.

Deviation (POL-RD-01). The trace ran 18.0 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km: an excess of 8.0 km (80% of optimal). Both establishment tests pass, so a deviation is established on this trip's own evidence.

Closure exoneration (POL-RD-03). The LTA advisory ADV-20260920-113 is genuine: it names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, a segment the booked optimal uses; its 18:14-18:55 window covers the 18:20-18:54 trip; and the actual route leaves the corridor and rejoins it. Exoneration is capped, however: the justified excess is min(8.0 km, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal is 13.60 km driven over 27.2 minutes, and the residual 4.40 km is the driver's to answer for. The rider accepted the closure; this cap is why the driver is not excused for the whole detour.

Materiality and driver profile (POL-RD-01 / POL-RD-06). On the surviving excess the deviation is 4.40 km against 13.60 km (32.4%), below the 50% limb, and 4.40 km is below the 8.0 km absolute limb, so the deviation is established but NOT material. No repeat-deviation pattern exists either: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 610 completed trips, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. (The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used for any finding.)

Fare (POL-RD-02). Charged total: SGD 31.42. Recomputed against the closure-adjusted route: (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 13.60 = 10.20 distance + 0.28 x 27.2 = 7.616 time) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP = SGD 23.416. Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = SGD 8.004, rounded UP to SGD 8.05. That clears the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 25.5% of the charged total, far short of the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a partial refund.

ERP (POL-RD-09). The SGD 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' line is off the optimal route and is already comprehended inside the SGD 8.05 recomputation (which credits only the on-optimal-route gantry); it is itemised for transparency and must not be added on top. Separately, the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' line charges for a gantry the GPS trace never passes: its closest fix is 834.18 m away, far outside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 sets for a crossing. Under POL-RD-09(4) that is a billing-integrity failure — refunded in full as a standalone correction (SGD 1.00) and referred for billing-integrity review. It does not engage POL-RD-10(8) because it is a line refunded under that limb. The rider therefore recovers SGD 8.05 + SGD 1.00 = SGD 9.05.

No artifact here carries a weight below 1.0, so no POL-GEN-02 disclosure discount applies, and confidence is not capped below the evidence's weight.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you accept that the closure was real; the question is how much of the completed route it excuses. Figures used: charged_total S$31.42; booked optimal 10.0 km / 20 min; completed route 18.0 km (the GPS trace governs, not the trip record's rounded copy), an excess of 8.0 km / 80%.

POL-RD-03 exoneration is capped, not open-ended. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, a segment the booked optimal route uses; its 18:14-18:55 window covers the 18:20-18:54 trip; and the route left the corridor and rejoined it. Justified excess = min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km. So 3.60 km is excused and 4.40 km is not.

POL-RD-02 then runs against the closure-adjusted optimal: 10.0 + 3.60 = 13.60 km, duration scaled to 27.2 min. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP = S$23.416. Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to S$8.05. That is 25.5% of the charge - above the S$0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share - so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of S$8.05. (Recomputing against the booked 10.0 km would give 18.70 and a 12.72 refund; that figure over-refunds because it does not excuse the closure, so it is not used.)

The S$2.80 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is off the optimal route; it is already comprehended in the 8.05, because the recomputed fare credits only the S$1.00 on-optimal-route ERP, so it is itemised for transparency but never added on top (POL-RD-09(1)). No driver compensation arises: the fare bills the full 18.0 km the trace records, so there is no unbilled distance.

Materiality and profile: the excess remaining after adjustment is 4.40 km / 32.4% of the adjusted optimal - below both material limbs - so POL-RD-06 is not engaged on materiality and no driver-conduct referral follows; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610, so no repeat pattern exists. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context-only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used; it appears only as a warning.

POL-RD-04 cannot be run: no chat message carries a waypoint_hint and the rider names no road, so its corroboration test is undecidable, the clause is unavailable, and the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

No escalation: the trace is intact (205 fixes, 10 s interval, no gaps, 100% coverage), so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) do not fire; trip identifiers and timestamps match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown; the refund is far below the disposal ceilings; and no exculpatory or profile argument rests on a missing artifact.

The surviving claims from both sides on the closure cap, the adjusted-route recomputation, the trace's integrity, the ERP treatment, the burden of proof, and the absence of a repeat-deviation pattern are accepted - they agree with the record and with each other. Confidence 0.90: every artifact carrying a deciding fact carries weight 1.0.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The trip on TRP-09113 ran 18.00 km against a booked optimal of 10.00 km, an excess of 8.00 km (80%). The GPS trace governs that measurement (POL-RD-01) and is unimpaired for policy purposes: 205 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) does not fire and no corroborating artifact is required; POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The rider's identity showing under POL-RD-08(a) is accepted (trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-09113), and the rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d = 0) adds no extra corroboration burden.

The LTA closure ADV-20260920-113 (Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, 18:14-18:55) overlaps the trip window, so POL-RD-03 exonerates part of the excess — but only up to its cap. The justified excess is the lesser of 8.00 km and 1.30 x (12.00 - 10.00) + 1.00 = 3.60 km. So 3.60 km is excused and 4.40 km is the driver's to answer for. The closure-adjusted optimal is 13.60 km, duration scaled to 27.2 minutes; the residual 4.40 km is 32.4% of 13.60 km, above the 20% / 0.8 km establishment tests but below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality limbs, so the deviation is established but NOT material and POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip. Even if it were reached, the driver's trailing-90-day record (deviation_flags_90d = 0 over 610 completed trips) shows no pattern and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags was mentioned only to say it is context-only under POL-GEN-01; that is correct, and no finding rests on it.

POL-RD-02 recomputation, run against the closure-adjusted route (not the booked one):
- charged_total: SGD 31.42
- recomputed_fare: SGD 23.416 (base 3.80 + distance 0.75 x 13.60 = 10.20 + time 0.28 x 27.2 = 7.616 + platform fee 0.80 + on-optimal-route ERP 1.00; no surge, promo or waiting fee)
- refund under POL-RD-02: 31.42 - 23.416 = SGD 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05.

POL-RD-04 adds nothing. The rider's chat instruction ('please take the lawful diversion') authorises the lawful 12.0 km diversion, not an 18 km route, so it cannot carry the 4.40 km of excess beyond the closure-adjusted route; and because neither message carries a waypoint_hint and no road is named, POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run — the clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. There is no unbilled-distance shortfall (billed 18.0 km equals the trace's 18.0 km), so no driver compensation arises.

ERP. The SGD 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' line is off the optimal route and is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure, which rebuilds the fare using only optimal-route gantries; it is itemised for transparency and is not added on top (POL-RD-09(1)). The SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' line is different: the GPS trace never passes that gantry — the closest fix is 834 m away, well outside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 sets — so it is a billing-integrity failure refunded in full as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4). It is the only unmatched line and it is refunded under that limb, so POL-RD-10(8) does not escalate the case.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND. Amount payable to the rider = 8.05 (POL-RD-02) + 1.00 (POL-RD-09(4) pass-through correction) = SGD 9.05. It clears the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and at about 25.5% of charged_total it is far short of the 90% full-refund share, so it is a partial refund, not a full one. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 is present.

Confidence: every artifact carrying a deciding fact — GPS trace, trip record, traffic advisory and fare breakdown — is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and none of the ruling rests on discounted or impaired evidence.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' ERP line is charged for a gantry the GPS trace never passes (closest fix 834 m from the gantry coordinates, outside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 sets); the line is refunded in full to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction.

ledger.claim: This is a single trip on the record, so the rider's initial burden of identity under POL-RD-08(a) is met: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-09113, and the trip_record's started_at (2026-09-20T18:20:00+08:00) matches the trace's first_fix_at to the second. There is no identifier mismatch and nothing to escalate under the identity limb.

The governing measurement is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 18.0 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 10.0 km, an excess of 8.0 km, or 80% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass with room to spare — the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km absolute — so a route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a max_gap_sec of 0. None of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires, so the excess stands on the trace alone and no independent corroborating artifact is required.

The rider accepts the closure, and the closure is real: LTA advisory ADV-20260920-113 names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, its validity window overlaps the trip, and it records a shortest lawful alternative of 12.0 km. But POL-RD-03 exoneration is capped, not open-ended: the justified excess is min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, and everything above that cap is the driver's to answer for.

Applying the POL-RD-03 cap produces a closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km (duration scaled to 27.2 minutes), and the trip still ran 18.0 km on the trace. The excess remaining after adjustment is 4.40 km — about 32% of the adjusted optimal and far above the 0.8 km absolute floor — so the deviation is still established on the adjusted route and the driver is not excused for it.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation runs against the closure-adjusted route, because POL-RD-03 excuses only part of the excess: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x surge 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the on-optimal-route gantry = 23.416 recompated against a charged_total of 31.42. The refund is therefore 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded UP to 8.05 payable.

The 8.004 refund is neither de minimis nor a full refund: it clears the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and at 25.5% of charged_total it falls well short of the 90% full-refund share, so the correct monetary outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-RD-02 — and because the payable figure rounds up to 8.05, it returns to the rider the entire SGD 8.05 that is contested in this dispute.

The only rider instruction on this record authorises the LAWFUL diversion, not an 18 km detour: at 18:23:10 the rider wrote 'please take the lawful diversion', and the shortest lawful alternative was 12.0 km. POL-RD-04 exonerates only the excess attributable to a rider instruction, so it cannot carry the 4.40 km of excess beyond the closure-adjusted route — the rider authorised the diversion, not an overrun of it.

POL-RD-04 is in any event unavailable to the driver on this record: neither chat message carries a waypoint_hint and the rider names no road, so the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 is undecidable, the clause cannot be run, and the case must be decided on the remaining clauses.

The rider's profile does not import any extra corroboration burden into POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the threshold of 4, so this claim is not one of those that must be supported beyond the gps_trace.

The S$2.80 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is flagged on_optimal_route false and is already comprehended inside the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which credits only the S$1.00 on-optimal-route gantry. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is itemised for transparency but must not be added on top of the 8.05 payable, and equally must not be netted down against it.

No part of this argument rests on discounted evidence: every artifact cited here carries admissibility status COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes, so no POL-GEN-02 disclosure discount applies and the deciding facts are carried by clean evidence.

The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 is a genuine external closure and exonerates part of the excess under POL-RD-03: it names 'Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector', a segment the booked optimal route traverses (the trip record's route source states the optimal was computed 'via Pelton Canal Link, the segment named in the LTA advisory'), its geometry intersects the route, and its 18:14-18:55 SGT validity window covers the 18:20-18:54 SGT trip. The justified excess is capped at min(8.0 km, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, so 3.60 km of the 8.0 km excess is excused and only the residual 4.40 km can be refunded to the rider.

Materiality under POL-RD-01 is assessed on the excess REMAINING after the POL-RD-03 adjustment, not on the excess as first measured. The surviving excess is 4.40 km against a closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km, i.e. 32.4%, which is below the 50% limb, and 4.40 km is also below the 8.0 km absolute limb. The deviation is therefore established but NOT material on this record, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile consequences and any driver-conduct referral are not triggered by this trip.

Even if POL-RD-06 is reached, no repeat-deviation pattern exists: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, which is not 3 or more, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d (610) is 0.00, which is not 0.05 or more, with completed_trips_90d far above the 40-trip floor. The lifetime counter driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are available on this profile.

ledger.claim: Once POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess, POL-RD-02 requires the fare to be recomputed against the closure-adjusted optimal route of 13.60 km / 27.2 min, not the booked 10.0 km / 20 min. On the adjusted route the recomputed fare is 23.416 (3.80 base + 10.20 distance + 7.616 time + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP; no surge, no promo, no waiting fee), so the refund is 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05 - the figure the fare breakdown already carries. Running the same clause against the booked optimal would yield 12.72 and would over-refund the rider by 4.72.

The off-route ERP line of SGD 2.80 at the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry (flagged on_optimal_route false) is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, which rebuilds the fare using only the on-optimal-route gantries (SGD 1.00 at the Pelton lawful diversion entry). Under POL-RD-09(1) the off-route charge is itemised for transparency but must NEVER be added on top of the refund, so the rider's total recovery on this dispute is capped at the POL-RD-02 figure.

The GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 - 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage and a maximum gap of 0 seconds - so it is impaired under none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation trigger is not engaged. The excess is accordingly measured exactly at 8.0 km on the governing trace distance, and nothing in the record supports a finding of any excess larger than the 4.40 km that survives the closure exoneration.

The chat log corroborates limb (c) of POL-RD-03 - that the actual route left the optimal corridor for the signed diversion and rejoined it - and dispels any suggestion of a driver frolic: at 18:22:40 the driver messaged that the Pelton Canal Link closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop, and at 18:23:10 the rider replied 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion.' The fare breakdown independently records the diversion-entry gantry as on the optimal route and the industrial-loop exit gantry as off it, matching the signed diversion the advisory describes.

The driver has discharged the burden that shifts to him under POL-RD-08 by naming a specific artifact and a specific clause - the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 and POL-RD-03 - rather than making a bare assertion that traffic was bad. The exoneration that follows is capped at 3.60 km, so the only sum properly refundable to the rider is the residual 4.40 km already reflected in the SGD 8.05 figure, and no greater sum may be awarded.
